analysis.summary: GrayC brings coverage-directed, mutation-based greybox fuzzing to C compilers and analysers, which have become relatively resistant to the blackbox fuzzers used until now. The difficulty is that naive mutations produce programs that do not compile and so cannot reach deep bugs. GrayC introduces mutations targeting common C constructs and transforms fuzzed programs so they produce meaningful output, enabling differential testing. It found 30 confirmed bugs, 25 previously unknown.
